Camden Council announces four schools face closure

15th October
Education
Kentish Town
By Bridget Galton Features Editor and Associate Editor

Share

0 comments
Read More
Four Camden schools face closure
amid falling pupil numbers and budget pressures
La Sainte Union in Highgate Road is a Catholic girls secondary school and part of the La Swap Sixth Form consortium but is pegged for closure. (Image: Wikimedia Commons)

0:00 / 2:21
Instaread

Four schools in Camden are under threat of closure due to falling pupil numbers and increased financial pressures.

Camden Council is inviting parents, staff and the wider community to have their say on proposals which would affect hundreds of primary and secondary pupils across the borough.

Cabinet members will decide on Tuesday, October 20 whether to launch public consultations about the future of St Alban's Church of England Primary School in Holborn, St Patrick's Catholic Primary School in Kentish Town, St Joseph's Catholic Primary School in Holborn, and La Sainte Union Catholic Secondary School in Highgate Road.

The authority says all the schools are are facing difficulties due to a slump in pupil numbers affecting schools across London citing falling birth rates, rising housing costs, and families relocating out of the capital.

Since school funding is linked to pupil numbers the empty places put pressure on budgets.

A statement put out by the council said both headteachers and Camden Council had tried to respond to the changes, but "high numbers of unfilled places and underused classrooms" were hitting the long-term sustainability of the schools.

The consultations will explore future options, giving parents, carers, staff, pupils, and local residents the chance to help shape the schools' future before decisions are made.

Councillor Marcus Boyland, cabinet member for best start for children and families, said: "Camden is a fantastic place to learn, and we are proud of our family of schools and staff, and the education they provide for local children.

"Beginning consultation on the future of individual schools is difficult, but we must respond to the challenges facing schools across London and take responsible steps to protect high-quality education both now and in the future.

"We want to work closely with parents, carers, staff, pupils, and local communities to understand their views and ideas before any decisions are made.

"These consultations will be an

opportunity
for everyone affected to help shape the future of these schools and make sure every Camden child can learn, make friends, and succeed in a thriving school environment."

If councillors agree, the consultation will begin on Monday, November 2, and run for six weeks including online information, surveys, and engagement events.

Special attention will be given to supporting children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND).

For full details of the proposals go to camden.gov.uk/SchoolProposals.
